title: California security deposit cap, one month's rent
requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value greater than one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.

applicability.other: residential property used as the dwelling of the tenant

exemptions: Advance payment of at least six months’ rent on a lease term of six months or longer; tenant-requested alterations; two months’ rent for qualifying small landlords; security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5: security deposit cap, one month’s rent
quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

title: California two months' rent security cap for small landlords
requirement: A landlord who is a natural person or an all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units may demand security up to two months’ rent, in addition to the first month’s rent.
coverage_conditions: Landlord is a natural person or an LLC in which all members are natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.

applicability.other: no more than two residential rental properties

exemptions: Does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5: two months’ rent cap, small landlord
quoted_span: (5) (A) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements:

title: California service member higher security, statement and return
requirement: On or after April 1, 2025, a landlord charging a service member a higher than standard security because of credit history, credit score, housing history or a similar factor must give a written statement of the amount and the reason by the date the lease is signed, and must return the additional amount after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in rent arrears.
coverage_conditions: Service members who rent residential property in which the service member will reside.

applicability.other: prospective or current tenant is a service member

citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5: service member higher security, statement and return
quoted_span: (4) On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.

title: California security return and itemization, 21 calendar days
requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of any security received and its disposition, with copies of documents showing charges incurred, and return the remaining portion.
coverage_conditions: Any tenancy of residential property in which the landlord holds security, subject to the notice and lease-expiration timing in subdivision (h).
exemptions: Documentation duties do not apply if deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed $125 or the tenant waived those rights; a good faith estimate may be used if repairs or documents cannot be completed within 21 days.
penalty: A landlord is not entitled to claim any amount of the security if the landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply with subdivision (h).
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5: return of security, 21 calendar days and itemized statement
quoted_span:
(h) (1) No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to
the expiration of a fixed-term lease, the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:

title: California photographs of the unit for security deductions
requirement: Beginning April 1, 2025 the landlord must photograph the unit after possession is returned but before any repair or cleaning deducted from the security, and again after the work; for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, photographs must also be taken at the inception of the tenancy.
coverage_conditions: Tenancies of residential property in which the landlord holds security under Section 1950.5.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5: photographs of the unit, inception and after possession returned
quoted_span: (2) Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.

title: California bad faith retention of security, statutory damages
requirement: A landlord or successor who in bad faith claims or retains a security deposit, or in bad faith demands replacement security, may be liable for statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security plus actual damages, and bears the burden of proof as to reasonableness.
key_value: 2x the amount of the security, plus actual damages
coverage_conditions: Any landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest holding security under Section 1950.5.
exemptions: A successor in interest with a good faith belief that the remaining security was transferred or returned is not liable for these damages.
penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages; the court may award bad faith damages whenever the facts warrant, even if not requested.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5: bad faith claim or retention, statutory damages
quoted_span: (m) The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

title: California ban on nonrefundable security provisions
requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not contain any provision characterizing a security deposit as nonrefundable.
coverage_conditions: Any lease or rental agreement for residential property under Section 1950.5.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5: nonrefundable security characterization prohibited
quoted_span: (n) A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

title: California application screening fee cap
requirement: A landlord or agent may charge an applicant a screening fee only up to the actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information about the applicant, and in no case more than thirty dollars per applicant, adjusted annually for the Consumer Price Index.
key_value: $30 per applicant, adjusted annually by CPI
coverage_conditions: Any applicant who requests to rent residential property from a landlord or the landlord’s agent.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6: application screening fee cap
quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

title: California bar on screening fees when no unit is available
requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
coverage_conditions: Any applicant who requests to rent residential property from a landlord or the landlord’s agent.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6: screening fee prohibited when no unit is available
quoted_span: (1) A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

title: California application screening fee refund conditions
requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if it offers a process that refunds applicants whose application is not considered or who are not selected, within seven days, or within seven days of selecting a tenant or thirty days of submission, whichever occurs first.
coverage_conditions: Any applicant charged an application screening fee by a landlord or the landlord’s agent.
exemptions: No refund required for an applicant denied after consideration for failing to meet the landlord’s established screening criteria.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6: screening fee refund requirements
quoted_span: (B) An application screening process in which the landlord or their agent returns the entire screening fee to any applicant who is not selected for tenancy, regardless of the reason, within 7 days of selecting an applicant for tenancy or 30 days of when the application was submitted, whichever occurs first.

title: California screening fee receipt and credit report copy
requirement: A landlord who charges a screening fee must give the applicant a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent, return any amount of the fee not used for authorized purposes, and provide a copy of the consumer credit report within seven days of receiving it.
coverage_conditions: Any applicant who paid an application screening fee to a landlord or the landlord’s agent.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6: screening fee receipt and credit report disclosure
quoted_span: The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.

title: California application processing order and first qualified applicant
requirement: A landlord charging a screening fee must consider completed applications in the order received under written screening criteria provided with the application form, and must approve the first applicant who meets those established criteria.
coverage_conditions: Applicants screened by a landlord or the landlord’s agent that charges an application screening fee.

applicability.other: applies when a landlord or agent charges an application screening fee

citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6: application processing order and first-qualified-applicant approval
quoted_span:
(i) Completed applications are considered, as provided for in the landlord’s established screening criteria, in the order in which the completed applications were received. The landlord’s screening criteria shall be provided to the applicant in writing together with the application form.
(ii) The first applicant who meets the landlord’s established screening criteria is approved for tenancy.

title: California source of income housing discrimination ban
requirement: The owner of any housing accommodation may not discriminate against or harass any person because of source of income, which includes public assistance and federal, state or local housing subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers.
coverage_conditions: Any housing accommodation and its owner.
exemptions: Making a written or oral inquiry concerning the level or source of income does not constitute discrimination based on source of income.
citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955: source of income discrimination
quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.

title: California income standard, aggregate income of co-tenants
requirement: A landlord may not use a financial or income standard in renting housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons living together on the same basis as the aggregate income of married persons living together.
coverage_conditions: Any rental of housing in which a financial or income standard is applied.
citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955: income standard, aggregate income of unmarried co-tenants
quoted_span:
(n) To use a financial or income standard in the rental of housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income
of married persons residing together or proposing to reside together.

title: California credit history alternative evidence with rent subsidy
requirement: Where a government rent subsidy is involved, a housing provider using a person’s credit history must offer the applicant the option of providing lawful verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant’s portion of rent, and must reasonably consider it in lieu of credit history.
coverage_conditions: Instances in which there is a government rent subsidy; the income standard must be based on the portion of rent to be paid by the tenant.

applicability.other: applies where there is a government rent subsidy

exemptions: Does not limit the owner’s ability to request information or documentation to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify the identity of a person.
citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955: credit history, alternative evidence of ability to pay
quoted_span:
(B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

title: California retaliatory eviction prohibited
requirement: An owner of housing accommodations may not harass, evict or otherwise discriminate against a person in the sale or rental of housing when the owner’s dominant purpose is retaliation for opposing unlawful practices or participating in a proceeding under this part.
citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955: retaliatory eviction prohibited
quoted_span: For any owner of housing accommodations to harass, evict, or otherwise discriminate against any person in the sale or rental of housing accommodations when the owner’s dominant purpose is retaliation against a person who has opposed practices unlawful under this section
